text:
Alex W.: quick follow-up to the offload RFC — thinking about switching from a long-lived pinned host staging pool to ephemeral NUMA-aware mmap() buffers that we populate on demand. main goal: reduce pinned memory footprint and fragmentation across tenants. open question: latency tail for cold pages and allocator interface changes. any red flags?

Maria L.: cold page faults are the obvious one. MAP_POPULATE helps but costs at alloc time. hugepages reduce page fault cost but complicate multi-tenant packing. also need to watch page cache churn if these buffers get swapped. :thinking:

Sanjay R.: fragmentation angle: if we mmap lots of variable-size host buffers we'll still fragment the process vma/anon ranges. suggestion: keep per-NUMA arenas + a small fixed-size page-slab allocator on top of mmap to serve hot small evictions. that lets us coalesce/compact within arena before touching pinned pool.

Kate: kernel OOM is scary if we rely on mlock too broadly. I think only hot KV entries should be mlocked/pinned; ephemeral mmaps can be unpinned unless we hit latency SLOs. need clear fallback: if page-fault latency > threshold, escalate to pinned fallback.

Alex W.: here's a quick config sketch for the idea:

```json
{
  "host_pool": {
    "mode": "ephemeral_mmap",
    "numa_arenas": 2,
    "arena_size_mb": 512,
    "slab_size_kb": 64,
    "page_populate": "on_demand",
    "pinned_fallback_threshold_ms": 8
  }
}
```

alloc-bot: perf-run results from last night: synthetic small-batch infer (32batches) shows ~12% throughput regression on cold-starts with ephemeral mmap vs pinned pool. tail latency (99.9th) spikes in first 5s of workload. full logs: http://ci/reports/1820012345/logs. (automated)

Maria L.: we should add telemetry: per-alloc page_fault_count, mmap_latency_hist, mlock_failures, numa_balancing_migrations. with those we can gate the fallback automatically. i'll add counters to the allocator shim.

Sanjay R.: API idea: Allocator::reserve(host_bytes, numa_hint, require_pinned=false) -> handle. caller can pass require_pinned=true when latency-critical. that keeps caller-level control and keeps the allocator able to optimize behind the scenes. also need a reclaim hint API: handle->hint_accessed() for eviction ranking.

Kate: +1 to reserve API. also add a safety quota per-worker so one model can't soak all pinned memory. quota_exhaustion -> best-effort fallback to mmap + degrade mode note in logs.

Alex W.: good input. next steps: i'll open a short follow-up RFC with explicit tradeoffs (latency vs pinned footprint vs fragmentation), pseudocode for the allocator API, perf test plan (cold-start and steady-state), and telemetry dashboard sketch. @Maria @Sanjay can you own perf runs and API draft? i'll stub the RFC tonight. :thumbsup:

Maria L.: happy to run perf and add counters. will start with synthetic traces (varying seq len & batch sizes) and short mortals.

Sanjay R.: i'll draft the allocator APIs and a small reference impl for per-NUMA arenas. will include reclaim hints and the pinned-fallback toggle.

Alex W.: great — thanks. i'll tag this thread into the RFC PR when created. if anyone sees an immediate blocker (security/KMS or kernel flags) shout here.

alloc-bot: note: CI job alloc-integration-tests will run on the RFC PR and will collect mmap/pin metrics automatically.
